observation.strongest_observed_fact: The two uploaded filesystem objects have different names but exactly identical JPEG byte streams.

mechanism.filesystem_identity: A pathname/filename is an external reference and metadata context for a file object; it is not automatically part of the file's content byte stream.
mechanism.sha256_input_contract: SHA256(file) hashes the bytes supplied as input. It does not include filename/path unless the caller explicitly concatenates or serializes that metadata into the hashed input.
mechanism.representation_law: IDENTITY DEPENDS ON REPRESENTATION: path/name representation distinguishes the two objects; raw-byte representation collapses them into the same equivalence class.

representation_contract.target_invariant_I: content identity independent of external labels
must_destroy_or_ignore: external label unless explicitly included in the input contract
representation_contract.metric: direct byte equality; SHA256 equality as an efficient index/witness, followed by direct equality for proof-critical use
representation_contract.positive_control: same bytes under renamed/copied files must collapse
representation_contract.negative_control: one-byte mutation must no longer be byte-equal and will overwhelmingly produce a different SHA256
representation_contract.falsifier: If direct byte comparison differs, the claim that the two files are content-identical is false even if some non-content metadata matches.
representation_contract.multiplicity_rule: Do not select a content representation post hoc merely because it collapses an inconvenient distinction; the target invariant must be frozen first.
representation_contract.provenance: Two current-conversation uploads inspected directly from mounted sandbox paths.
representation_contract.unknown_rule: Hash collision is a theoretical possibility; for proof-critical equality, retain direct byte equality rather than treating SHA256 equality alone as a mathematical proof of identity.

complexity_hypothesis.name: INVARIANT_PRESERVING_QUOTIENT_STATE_SPACE
complexity_hypothesis.idea: If a search problem contains many syntactically distinct states that are equivalent with respect to the invariant relevant to the decision problem, a canonical representation may collapse them into one quotient state and prevent redundant exploration.
complexity_hypothesis.equivalence_relation: x ~_I y iff x and y are indistinguishable with respect to the target invariant I under a proven preservation contract.
potential_benefits: proof reuse across differently labeled but invariant-equivalent states
search DAG compression instead of path-tree repetition
complexity_hypothesis.critical_boundary: THIS OBSERVATION DOES NOT BY ITSELF ESTABLISH A POLYNOMIAL-TIME ALGORITHM OR P=NP.
what_would_be_required_for_a_polynomial_: Define the exact target invariant I for the computational problem.
Construct a canonicalizer C(x) computable in polynomial time.
Prove x ~_I y iff C(x)=C(y), or prove the weaker equivalence needed for safe pruning.
Prove every legal transition respects the equivalence relation, so quotienting cannot delete a necessary witness.
Prove the number of reachable equivalence classes is polynomially bounded in input size, or otherwise prove the quotient exploration is polynomial.
Provide a polynomial-size proof/certificate that each pruning/merge preserves correctness.
Adversarially test cases where labels differ but semantics do not, and cases where superficially similar states differ on the target invariant.
failure_modes: Canonicalization itself may be as hard as the original problem.
The quotient may still contain exponentially many equivalence classes.
An overly coarse representation may merge states that differ on witness existence.
SHA256 cannot serve as the semantic canonicalizer unless the invariant is exact byte identity; it destroys most higher-level structure by design.

next_gate.name: APPLY_QUOTIENT_OPERATOR_TO_CURRENT_P_N_SEARCH_GRAMMAR
next_gate.required_output: Identify one concrete family of currently distinct search states in the active P/N proof engine that may be equivalent under the decision invariant, define a polynomial canonical representative, and test whether quotienting reduces reachable state count without deleting known witnesses or legal successors.

canonical_seal: TWO NAMES CAN DENOTE ONE CONTENT WITNESS. THE COMPUTATIONAL OPPORTUNITY IS NOT THE HASH ITSELF, BUT THE PROVEN RIGHT TO COLLAPSE MANY LABELLED STATES INTO ONE INVARIANT-PRESERVING EQUIVALENCE CLASS. THE POLYNOMIAL QUESTION BEGINS ONLY AFTER THAT COLLAPSE IS PROVED SAFE AND POLYNOMIALLY BOUNDED.
